findings.claim: Read-AgyEvents exempts the final non-empty line from malformed-stream detection regardless of exit status, so a completed run with a valid result plus trailing corruption can be ingested.
findings.trigger: A fake or real agy stream has one valid result followed by a truncated or non-JSON final line while the process exits 0.

evidence.observation: The parser skips malformed parsing for the last non-empty line without checking whether the run was killed.
All real streams contain exactly one result and matching init/result conversation ids; the edge is not represented.

findings.verification: Append garbage after a valid fake-agy result and assert that Read-AgyEvents reports malformed.
findings.remedy: Ignore a trailing partial line only when a timeout/pre-failure is present; otherwise reject the stream.

history.note: Read-AgyEvents -AllowPartialLast only after a kill or a non-zero exit; garbage after a valid result on exit 0 is a malformed stream (class transport)

findings.claim: When several roster entries share one provider label, `-Provider <label>` without `-Model` silently selects the first entry, which can choose the wrong tier.
findings.trigger: A roster contains `gemini` low-tier and `gemini` weighty high-tier entries and the caller passes only `-Provider gemini`.

evidence.observation: The documented selection rule is the first entry of that provider.
The listing test intentionally creates two gemini entries with different models.

findings.verification: Dry-run `-Provider gemini` with that roster and inspect the selected model.
findings.remedy: Require `-Model` when a label is non-unique, or record and display a prominent first-entry selection warning.

history.note: -Provider <label> without -Model on a non-unique label warns on the console and in warnings[] naming the entry used
